days.label: Today
days.note: Best morning of the next three. W offshore holds till noon and the tide runs in off an 8:21am low — but the swell is dead-south (167°), so Dee Why is the small one. Long Reef is a clear foot bigger for the same energy.

dee-why.window: 8–11am. Offshore W 10 km/h, tide filling off the 8:21am low (0.46m). Energy peaks around 106 kJ at first light and fades to 73 by noon — go early, not at 11.

tip.label: Beachie over Point
tip.text: 167° is the direction the Point can't use — expect it fat and gutless. The ENE windswell at 64° is doing the real work, so the beachie banks will have more shape than the Point today. Save the frontside rights for Sunday's E/NE.

swells.label: Dominant SSE — Long Reef's best-exposed angle of the four

long-reef.window: 8–11am. Biggest on the coast today — 3–4ft while Dee Why sits at 2–3, off identical offshore energy. Incoming tide off the low switches the reef bowl on.

tip.label: Take the drive
tip.text: The extra foot is real, not a rating artefact — same 98 kJ, better exposure to the 167° swell. You're backside on the lefts off the point, so pick the corner that lets you set a rail early rather than chasing the end section.

curl-curl.window: Dawn–10am. 3–4ft on the sets at first light, easing to 2–3 by mid-morning as energy drops from 114 kJ to 98. Second-best of the four today.

tip.label: Go at first light
tip.text: Curl Curl handles the S angle better than Dee Why but loses it fast — the 6am reading is a full size step above 9am. If you're not in the water by 7:30 it's a Long Reef day instead.

swells.label: Dominant SSE — shadowed badly at North Steyne
ENE windswell, the only thing keeping it rideable

manly.window: Morning only, and it's the smallest of the four — down to knee–thigh by mid-afternoon. Fine for an easy uncrowded paddle, not a session worth planning.

tip.label: Skip unless it's convenience
tip.text: North Steyne is shadowed from a 167° swell and drops to 1–2ft by 6pm. Nothing here today that Long Reef isn't doing twice as well.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Smaller and softer — the S swell has faded to 2.5ft @ 8s from 176°, dead south. W offshore holds till around noon, then a hard E/NE sea breeze builds to 16 gusting 28 km/h and shuts it down. Strictly a dawn-to-10am job.

dee-why.window: Dawn–10am. 58 kJ and a 176° dead-south swell is the worst combination for this beach. Ratings slide to poor–fair from midday as the NE fills.

long-reef.window: Pick of Saturday. 3–4ft on the sets around 9am while everywhere else sits at 2–3. In by 9, out by 11.
alerts: NE sea breeze builds to 16 gusting 28 km/h from mid-afternoon

curl-curl.window: Dawn–10am while the W offshore holds. Drops to poor by mid-afternoon once the NE is on it.

manly.window: Knee to thigh all day. Not a session — a swim.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is leftovers. Sunday is the day: a new E/NE swell arrives from 70° and swings to 55° — exactly the 30–80° window Dee Why wants — filling from 3.1ft @ 9s at dawn to 4.4ft by noon, 5.1ft by 6pm and 6.6ft by nightfall, into a chest-to-overhead Monday. Light NW–N offshore early Sunday, going cross-shore N by 9am. Surf Sunday morning for clean, or hang around for size.

dee-why.window: Sunday 7–10am. NW offshore at dawn going N cross-shore by 9. Energy triples through the day (87 kJ at 9am → 302 by noon → 522 by 9pm) as the swing to 55° kicks in — a rare direction win for this beach. Late Sunday is the sleeper session.
alerts: Swell builds hard through Sunday afternoon — size steps up fast

long-reef.window: Best-rated slot of the whole weekend — fair-to-good at 6am Sunday on the light NW offshore. Builds to waist–shoulder by afternoon and chest-to-overhead by Monday dawn.
alerts: Monday morning is shaping up bigger again — 7ft @ 8s from 56°

curl-curl.window: Sunday 7–10am. Picks up the new E/NE cleanly and holds 3–4ft through the day, touching fair-to-good early Monday.
alerts: Swell builds hard through Sunday afternoon

manly.window: Sunday morning only — 2–3ft and rated poor through the afternoon once the N cross-shore is on it. The northern spots are handling this swell far better.
